question: Zomato on-campus Machine Learning Engineer interview (Aug 2025, Glassdoor report). One of the questions: **what is the difference between BERT-based text embeddings and Word2Vec?**
lookingFor: Grasp of static vs contextual representations
Knowing how each model is trained
Awareness of practical trade-offs (cost, out-of-vocabulary handling, use cases)
Ability to give a concrete example, not only definitions
answer:
**Core difference: static vs contextual.** Word2Vec (skip-gram or CBOW) learns one fixed vector per word type. BERT produces a different vector for every token occurrence, depending on the whole sentence.

Example: "bank" in "river bank" and "bank account" has the same Word2Vec vector (a blend of its senses) but different BERT vectors.

**Training.**
- Word2Vec: a shallow network (one hidden/projection layer) trained to predict a word from its neighbours (CBOW) or neighbours from a word (skip-gram), with negative sampling or hierarchical softmax. Training is cheap and fast.
- BERT: a deep bidirectional Transformer encoder pre-trained with masked language modelling (predict masked tokens using left and right context) and next-sentence prediction (dropped in later variants). It is very expensive to pre-train, but the weights are then reused.

**Vocabulary.** Word2Vec has a word-level vocabulary, so unseen words are out-of-vocabulary (you need a fallback or a variant like fastText with subwords). BERT uses WordPiece subword tokens, so any word can be represented by pieces.

**Using them.** Word2Vec vectors are lookups and are cheap, so they work as features for simple classifiers, similarity and recommendations, particularly with small compute budgets. BERT embeddings are read from a layer's output (for example the `[CLS]` token or mean pooling) or the model is fine-tuned end to end, and they usually give better accuracy on tasks that need context, such as NER, QA and sentiment with negation. Note that raw BERT outputs are not ideal sentence embeddings; models like Sentence-BERT are fine-tuned for that.

**Trade-offs.** BERT costs far more in memory and latency (hundreds of millions of parameters vs a lookup table) and has a fixed input length (512 tokens). Word2Vec can be good enough for simple, latency-critical or low-resource problems.
